objective: Partition with an honest type predicate in one ordered pass, returning independent typed branch arrays.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Type predicates, generics and Exclude remain current TypeScript tools.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Splitting typed unions is practical data processing.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Guard promises, callback cardinality and result independence transfer to validators.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The fourth cumulative stage adds a bounded conditional-type application.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Calling an effectful predicate twice can duplicate work and disagree between branches.

defects: The senior board used two filter passes and called the guard twice.
The brief did not explain that the Exclude return relies on a two-sided honest guard.
Callback order/arity/receiver and independent empty/matched/rest ownership were untested.
rationale: Rewrite only the senior partition fragment to one typed reduce pass, preserving earlier senior helpers and the reference/indexed boards. State that predicates must be true iff membership in S, so a positive-number refinement is not a guard for all numbers; the API does not validate arbitrary supplied predicates. Three new runtime assertions inspect exact single-pass call sequence/receiver/arity, object references, independent tuple/branch arrays across calls, errors and1000 mixed items. A new discriminated-union static case confirms both result branches while retaining old mismatched tuple rejection. The original two-filter senior is the meaningful wrong program: it passed old checks and now fails callback evidence. Earlier nine new assertions and all old checks remain cumulative. Target O(n) excluding callback internals.

objective: Sort a fresh generic array stably by bounded homogeneous key tuples while preserving the earlier helper contracts.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Typed rest selectors and stable copying sorts remain current collection patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Multi-key sorting is practical table/data preparation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Comparator consistency, UTF-16 ordering and opaque references transfer to other orderings.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The fifth cumulative stage combines earlier generic helpers with a bounded comparison model.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Mixed/NaN keys or invoking selectors as array methods can break comparator consistency or callback expectations.

defects: Numeric/string homogeneity, NaN handling and text comparison units were unstated.
The junior invoked keys[i] as a method, giving the selector the keys array as receiver.
No-key result freshness and equal-key object identity were insufficiently tested.
Returning the input directly when no selectors existed passed old checks.
rationale: Capture each junior selector in a local before calling it, and carry the repaired one-pass senior partition forward. Keep valid sort boards and add an indexed stable-decoration alternative. Define at most five deterministic same-type selectors, bounded finite numbers or UTF-16 strings, plain one-argument calls with unspecified comparison count/order, and errors. Four new runtime assertions cover fresh zero-key/empty/singleton copies, stable reference-preserving tuple ties, raw Unicode order, selector receiver/arity, source preservation/error and1000 records. A readonly-row/mutable-output static assertion complements the missing-selector-property negative. Twelve earlier new assertions and their static requirements remain cumulative, giving16 distinct added runtime assertions (46 executions across five stages) and five distinct added static assertions (15 cumulative executions). O(n log n) uses the explicit comparison-sort/constant-selector model, not measured engine asymptotics.
